title: Server-side rendering of untrusted MDX is a demonstrated code-execution class, not a theoretical one
statement: CVE-2026-0969 (GHSA-g4xw-jxrg-5f6m, GitHub-reviewed, high severity) records arbitrary code execution during React server-side rendering of untrusted MDX: the `serialize` function used to compile MDX in `next-mdx-remote` was vulnerable due to insufficient sanitisation of MDX content. Versions from 4.3.0 up to 6.0.0 are affected and 6.0.0 is the first patched release.
notes: ⚠️ THE VULNERABLE LIBRARY IS NOT THE ONE THIS PROJECT WOULD USE, and saying so is the difference between evidence and alarm. `next-mdx-remote` compiles MDX at RUNTIME from a supplied string; `@next/mdx` compiles at BUILD time from files in the repository. The exposure is not the same and this CVE does not transfer directly. ⚠️ WHAT DOES TRANSFER IS THE MECHANISM. The vulnerability was not a bug in a parser — it is what AST-0023 already established, arriving as an incident: MDX expressions and ESM are code, so compiling a document IS executing its author's intent. `next-mdx-remote` was only the place that property met an untrusted author first. ⚠️ It answers the question this was held open for: whether anyone had run semi-trusted MDX and what went wrong. Someone did, and it was CWE-94.
